line: Let’s explore triangles
spoken: Let’s explore triangles

line: Before we return to the tunnel, learn how to recognise them.
spoken: Before we return to the tunnel, learn how to recognise them.

line: Triangles can look different.
spoken: Triangles can look different.

line: Let’s explore what makes them triangles.
spoken: Let’s explore what makes them triangles.

line: This is a triangle.
spoken: This is a triangle.

line: A triangle is a closed shape
spoken: A triangle is a closed shape

line: with three straight sides.
spoken: with three straight sides.

line: Triangles can have different shapes.
spoken: Triangles can have different shapes.

line: Let’s explore their sides.
spoken: Let’s explore their sides.

line: Let’s measure the sides of this triangle.
spoken: Let’s measure the sides of this triangle.

line: What do you notice about the sides?
spoken: What do you notice about the sides?

line: All three are different
spoken: All three are different

line: Two sides are equal
spoken: Two sides are equal

line: All three are equal
spoken: All three are equal

line: Look at the side lengths again.
spoken: Look at the side lengths again.

line: Yes! 5 cm, 4 cm and 6 cm are all different.
spoken: Yes! five centimetres, four centimetres and six centimetres are all different.

line: All three sides are different.
spoken: All three sides are different.

line: A triangle with all three sides different is called a scalene triangle.
spoken: A triangle with all three sides different is called a scalene triangle.

line: What if two sides were equal?
spoken: What if two sides were equal?

line: All three are equal now. Make just two equal.
spoken: All three are equal now. Make just two equal.

line: Tip: make the two slanted sides show the same number.
spoken: Tip: make the two slanted sides show the same number.

line: Drag a vertex to make two sides equal.
spoken: Drag a vertex to make two sides equal.

line: Watch the numbers change as you drag.
spoken: Watch the numbers change as you drag.

line: Two sides are equal.
spoken: Two sides are equal.

line: A triangle with two equal sides is called an isosceles triangle.
spoken: A triangle with two equal sides is called an isosceles triangle.

line: Tip: the base is the third side — make the other two match it.
spoken: Tip: the base is the third side, make the other two match it.

line: Can you make all three sides equal?
spoken: Can you make all three sides equal?

line: Drag a vertex until the three lengths match.
spoken: Drag a vertex until the three lengths match.

line: All three sides are equal.
spoken: All three sides are equal.

line: A triangle with all three sides equal is called an equilateral triangle.
spoken: A triangle with all three sides equal is called an equilateral triangle.

line: Challenge time.
spoken: Challenge time.

line: Make this triangle isosceles.
spoken: Make this triangle isosceles.

line: All three sides are equal — make exactly two equal.
spoken: All three sides are equal, make exactly two equal.

line: Hint: drag the top vertex until two sides show the same length.
spoken: Hint: drag the top vertex until two sides show the same length.

line: Great! This triangle is isosceles.
spoken: Great! This triangle is isosceles.

line: Sort the triangles by their sides.
spoken: Sort the triangles by their sides.

line: Drag a triangle into its group — or tap a triangle, then tap a group.
spoken: Drag a triangle into its group, or tap a triangle, then tap a group.

line: Great job! You sorted all the triangles.
spoken: Great job! You sorted all the triangles.

line: Now let’s measure the angles.
spoken: Now let’s measure the angles.

line: What do you notice about the angles?
spoken: What do you notice about the angles?

line: All are acute angles
spoken: All are acute angles

line: One angle is a right angle
spoken: One angle is a right angle

line: One angle is obtuse
spoken: One angle is obtuse

line: Check the angles once more.
spoken: Check the angles once more.

line: Yes! All three are acute angles.
spoken: Yes! All three are acute angles.

line: All three angles are less than 90°.
spoken: All three angles are less than ninety degrees.

line: So they are acute angles.
spoken: So they are acute angles.

line: A triangle with three acute angles is called an acute-angled triangle.
spoken: A triangle with three acute angles is called an acute angled triangle.

line: Tip: find an angle in the 80s and keep opening it.
spoken: Tip: find an angle in the eighties and keep opening it.

line: Can you make one angle exactly 90°?
spoken: Can you make one angle exactly ninety degrees?

line: Drag a vertex — the angles change live.
spoken: Drag a vertex, the angles change live.

line: One angle is exactly 90°.
spoken: One angle is exactly ninety degrees.

line: A triangle with one angle of exactly 90° is called a right-angled triangle.
spoken: A triangle with one angle of exactly ninety degrees is called a right angled triangle.

line: What if one angle were greater than 90°?
spoken: What if one angle were greater than ninety degrees?

line: Tip: open one corner wider than a square corner.
spoken: Tip: open one corner wider than a square corner.

line: Drag a vertex to make any angle obtuse.
spoken: Drag a vertex to make any angle obtuse.

line: Make one corner wider than a right angle.
spoken: Make one corner wider than a right angle.

line: One angle is greater than 90°.
spoken: One angle is greater than ninety degrees.

line: A triangle with one angle greater than 90° is called an obtuse-angled triangle.
spoken: A triangle with one angle greater than ninety degrees is called an obtuse angled triangle.

line: Which of these are acute-angled triangles?
spoken: Which of these are acute angled triangles?

line: You can choose more than one.
spoken: You can choose more than one.

line: Tap every triangle whose angles are all less than 90°.
spoken: Tap every triangle whose angles are all less than ninety degrees.

line: Correct! These two triangles have only acute angles.
spoken: Correct! These two triangles have only acute angles.

line: Hint: one angle must read exactly 90°.
spoken: Hint: one angle must read exactly ninety degrees.

line: Make this triangle right-angled.
spoken: Make this triangle right angled.

line: Drag any vertex to create one 90° angle.
spoken: Drag any vertex to create one ninety-degree angle.

line: A triangle with one 90° angle is right-angled.
spoken: A triangle with one ninety-degree angle is right angled.

line: What type of triangle is this by its sides?
spoken: What type of triangle is this by its sides?

line: Scalene
spoken: Scalene

line: Isosceles
spoken: Isosceles

line: Equilateral
spoken: Equilateral

line: Two sides are 5 cm. It is isosceles.
spoken: Two sides are five centimetres. It is isosceles.

line: Now classify the same triangle by its angles.
spoken: Now classify the same triangle by its angles.

line: Acute-angled
spoken: Acute angled

line: Right-angled
spoken: Right angled

line: Obtuse-angled
spoken: Obtuse angled

line: One angle is 90°. It is right-angled.
spoken: One angle is ninety degrees. It is right angled.

line: This triangle is isosceles…
spoken: This triangle is isosceles,

line: …and right-angled.
spoken: and right angled.

line: A triangle can be classified in two ways.
spoken: A triangle can be classified in two ways.

line: By its sides…
spoken: By its sides,

line: …and by its angles.
spoken: and by its angles.

line: Acute
spoken: Acute

line: Right
spoken: Right

line: Obtuse
spoken: Obtuse

line: Classify this triangle by its sides and angles.
spoken: Classify this triangle by its sides and angles.

line: Choose one answer in each row.
spoken: Choose one answer in each row.

line: Correct! This triangle is scalene and obtuse-angled.
spoken: Correct! This triangle is scalene and obtuse angled.

line: Final challenge.
spoken: Final challenge.

line: Make a right-angled isosceles triangle.
spoken: Make a right angled isosceles triangle.

line: You can classify triangles by sides and angles!
spoken: You can classify triangles by sides and angles!

line: Let’s summarise what we learned.
spoken: Let’s summarise what we learned.

line: A scalene triangle has all sides different.
spoken: A scalene triangle has all sides different.

line: An isosceles triangle has two equal sides.
spoken: An isosceles triangle has two equal sides.

line: An equilateral triangle has all three sides equal.
spoken: An equilateral triangle has all three sides equal.

line: An acute-angled triangle has all angles less than 90°.
spoken: An acute angled triangle has all angles less than ninety degrees.

line: A right-angled triangle has one angle of exactly 90°.
spoken: A right angled triangle has one angle of exactly ninety degrees.

line: An obtuse-angled triangle has one angle greater than 90°.
spoken: An obtuse angled triangle has one angle greater than ninety degrees.

line: A triangle can be classified by both its sides and its angles.
spoken: A triangle can be classified by both its sides and its angles.

line: Well done, triangle explorer!
spoken: Well done, triangle explorer!
